docs.purpose: The landing spot when someone taps the confirmation link in their sign-up email. It quietly exchanges the one-time code from the link for a real session and, when that works, the app routes them onward on its own. When it fails it explains which of two things went wrong: the link expired or was already used, or the link was opened on a different device than the one they signed up on.
docs.data_story: This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device. It holds no client-side store, so there is no local copy of server state to keep in sync. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.
docs.under_126: **LEAVE ALONE — deliberately out of scope.** This screen talks to the Supabase Auth SDK, not to our contracts, so a descriptor would be describing someone else's protocol. Spec 126's Operating Boundaries fence it explicitly.

tables: mobile/src/lib/confirmEmail.ts:65 — GoTrue writes auth.users/auth.sessions; no application table is touched
emits: mobile/app/(auth)/confirm.tsx:1-91 — no track() call in the file

identity.owner: unassigned (no CODEOWNERS file and no owner registry exists in the repo — measured 2026-09-15)

versioning.why: Its only input is a one-time PKCE code in a route param and its only output is a Supabase session; nothing consumes a shape from this screen.

inputs.why: The `?code=` param is handed to it by the root layout's EmailConfirmLinkCatcher, which is the only thing that can route here; the screen reaches no API contract and no device sensor.

outputs.why: A successful exchange writes a Supabase session into the auth client's on-device AsyncStorage; the app's own API is never called from this screen.
outputs.rollback: none — the PKCE code is single-use; a failed exchange is terminal and the screen offers a route back to sign-in rather than a retry.

state.why: It holds only React component state (`status`) and a single-use ref guard — the state vocabulary has no value for component-local useState, so the honest answer is that it owns no Layer 2-5 state.

staleness.why: No server projection is displayed — the screen is a spinner and two terminal messages.

session.why: It is reachable with no session at all — establishing one is the point. It projects no data field, so there is nothing to disclose.

rls_class.why: It reaches no application table; the session write is GoTrue's.

disclosure.why: Anonymous, but it renders no server-sourced field at all — only fixed copy and the outcome of the code exchange.

guards.rate_bucket: none — no app route is called; GoTrue owns the exchange throttle

checks.why: mobile/__tests__/confirmEmail.test.ts locks BOTH declared failure reasons — generic invalid/expired and the PKCE same-device case — which the screen renders with different copy and different testIDs.
attemptedRef makes the exchange fire exactly once; a second attempt would burn a one-time code on a fast-refresh or a param identity change (confirm.tsx:33-37).
confirmEmail.test.ts pins parseConfirmDeepLink, the pure parser the root-layout catcher uses to decide whether a URL belongs to this screen at all.
The single Pressable carries a role and a label; there is nothing else to label.

errors.why: Both failures render full-screen inline copy with a route back to sign-in; there is no envelope because no app API is called.

emits.why: Email confirmation — the last step of the sign-up funnel — emits no event, so the drop-off between signup_completed and a live session is invisible.

offers.why: No sponsored placement is rendered: the only slot component in the Expo tree is SponsorSlot, and it returns null unless EXPO_PUBLIC_PARCEL_SPONSORS=1.

metering.why: Nothing here is counted: the Spec 126 §7 usage ledger table does not exist (grep for usage_events in the introspected drizzle schema returns 0 hits), and the only quota-shaped counter, user_profiles.lead_views_count, is incremented solely by POST /api/leads/view, which has no mobile caller.

config.why: The surface consumes no registered logic variable: the only server-side tunable in this path, user_profiles.radius_cap_km, is a per-user admin column, not a logic_variables row.

limitations.what: On success the screen never navigates — it keeps the spinner and waits for AuthGate to route away, so a routing regression would present as a permanent "Confirming your email…".
limitations.measured: confirm.tsx:45-48 — the ok branch deliberately does nothing, with a comment saying AuthGate routes away.

notes: Its route is reachable only via the root layout's Linking listener: expo-router maps maxbld://auth/confirm to /auth/confirm, which no file inside the (auth) group can match, so the catcher re-routes into /(auth)/confirm.

programme.why: Authentication. It talks to the Supabase Auth SDK and gates entry to both products; no product owns it.
